items.stem: In a merit-order electricity market, what sets the wholesale clearing price in each period?

options.text: The marginal cost of the most expensive plant needed to meet demand
options.rationale: The marginal (last dispatched) plant sets the clearing price for all.

options.text: The average cost of all plants running
options.rationale: Markets clear at the marginal, not the average, cost.
The cheapest sets the bottom of the stack, not the price.

options.text: A fixed government tariff per kWh
options.rationale: Competitive wholesale markets are not set by a fixed tariff.

items.explanation: The marginal (last dispatched) plant sets the clearing price for all.

items.stem: Which TWO are limitations of levelised cost of energy (LCOE) as a decision metric? (Select TWO.)

options.text: It ignores system costs such as balancing and transmission
options.rationale: LCOE omits integration and system costs.

options.text: It does not capture the value of when energy is delivered
options.rationale: LCOE treats all output as equal regardless of timing or value.

options.text: It cannot be calculated for any renewable technology
options.rationale: LCOE is routinely calculated for renewables.

options.text: It always equals the market clearing price
options.rationale: LCOE is a cost metric, not the market price.

items.explanation: LCOE omits integration and system costs.

items.stem: Why do economists argue a carbon price can improve market outcomes?

options.text: It internalises the external cost of emissions that the market otherwise ignores
options.rationale: Carbon pricing corrects an externality by making emitters pay its cost.

options.text: It guarantees the lowest possible electricity bills immediately
options.rationale: A carbon price may raise some prices in the short run.

options.text: It removes the need to measure emissions
options.rationale: Pricing requires measuring emissions, not removing the need.

options.text: It eliminates all market failures at once
options.rationale: It addresses the emissions externality, not every failure.

items.explanation: Carbon pricing corrects an externality by making emitters pay its cost.
